LANGUAGE BORROWING: ETYMOLOGY AND CHANGES IN MEANING AND PRONUNCIATION OF ARABIC VOCABULARY IN SWAHILI. When speakers of two languages come into contact and interact, those languages can directly borrow from and influence each other phonologically, lexically, and grammatically. When the Arabs arrived on the East African coast, they encountered the Swahili, and it was then that Swahili borrowed words and sounds from Arabic that did not previously exist in the Swahili language. Secondly, Swahili also adopted some Arabic sounds and modified the way they are pronounced. This article investigates and identifies the etymology of certain Arabic words found in the Swahili language and examines how Arabic sounds were borrowed, altered, and adapted into Swahili. Furthermore, it explores how the original meanings of some words changed after being borrowed from Arabic. Theoretical frameworks and cognitive semantics of vocabulary were applied. Introduction:- When Swahili came into contact with the Arabic language, it borrowed two things. It borrowed many Arabic words and adapted them, and secondly, it borrowed Arabic sounds that came with some of those words. The entry of Arabic words and sounds into the Swahili language resulted in two types of language change. The first type of change is the transformation or simplification of Arabic sounds so they can be pronounced by speakers of Swahili, which is a Bantu language. Secondly, there was a change in the original meaning of some Arabic words when they were incorporated into the Swahili language. This article will discuss language borrowing from Arabic into Swahili, the ways in which sound changes took place, and the alteration of the original meaning of some Arabic words borrowed into Swahili. This article employs two theories. The first is the structural theory, which deals with the changes in the sounds of words borrowed from the Arabic language. According to Mulder and Hervy (1975), this theory regards language as a large system comprised of many subsystems within it. They state that language is a system with five subsystems: semantics, pragmatics, syntax. Morphology and phonology. This article will focus on phonology, examining how sounds change. The second theory is that of cognitive lexical semantics. According to Paradis (2012), this theory deals with changes in meaning in words, which is one of the topics of this article. Hamisi Babusa. Address: Kenyatta University. Sound changes in borrowed Arabic words. Many Arabic words borrowed into the Swahili language, in addition to undergoing changes to adapt vowel patterns and conform to the structure of Swahili words, also experienced alterations to their original sounds. These sounds were changed because they did not exist at all in Swahili, and even if they had been borrowed directly, they would have caused pronunciation difficulties for Swahili speakers who were not accustomed to articulating these Arabic sounds. The following examples illustrate the changes in pronunciation of some Arabic words that have been incorporated into the Swahili language. Differentiation Between the Arabic ي (Yee) and the Swahili Vowel. The Arabic ي (Yee) or /y/ is the final consonant in the Arabic alphabet. There are some Arabic words that have a (yee) with a shadda. For example, MANIYYI منێ, NABIYYI نبێ, HAYYU حێ, TWAYYIB ﻄﯿﺐ, and MAYYITU مێټ. When these words were borrowed into Swahili, the ي (yee) was dropped and replaced by the vowel /i/. MANIYYI became MANII, NABIYYI became NABII. HAYYU became HAI, TWAYYIB became taib, MAYYITU became MAITI, etc.

Differentiation of the Arabic ع (‘Ain) and the Swahili Vowel

ﻉ (‘ain) is the eighteenth consonant in the Arabic alphabet. Some Arabic words that contain this sound include: ‘Aib عﯿﺐ, Mu‘allim معلم, ‘Ahdi عﻬد, ‘aqli عﻘل, and tis'a ﺗﺴعﺔ. When these words were borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, the Arabic ﻉ ‘ain, which is difficult for Africans to pronounce, was dropped and replaced with a vowel. For example, ‘aib became AIBU, mu’allim became MWALIMU, ‘ahdi became AHADI, ‘aqli became AKILI, and tis’a became TISA.

Change of ﻄ (Twee) in Arabic to /T/ in Swahili

Another sound change occurs where an Arabic word containing the ﻄ (twee) consonant is changed to /t/ after being borrowed into Swahili. For example, the following words are from Arabic: TWAYYIB ﻄﯿﺐ and TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ. When these words were borrowed and incorporated into the Swahili language, the ﻂ (twee) consonant was dropped and replaced with /t/, resulting in the Swahili words TARIKI and TAIB.

Change of ﺺ (Swaad) in Arabic to /S/ in Swahili

Arabic words that have the ﺺ (swaad) consonant, when entering the Swahili language, are changed so that ﺺ (swaad) becomes /s/. For example: SWAADIQ ﺻﺎدﻖ changed to SADIKI, SWAGHYR ﺻﻐﯿﺭ changed to SAGHIRI, and SWIRAAT ﺻﺮﺁﺖ changed to SIRATI.

Change of ﻖ (Qaaf) in Arabic to /K/ in Swahili

In the Arabic alphabet, there is ﻙ (kaaf) /k/ and ﻖ (qaaf). ﻖ (qaaf) is the twenty-first consonant in the Arabic alphabet, pronounced further back in the mouth than /k/, i.e., with contact at the soft palate and the back of the tongue. Bantu speakers did not have this sound, and when words with this Arabic sound were borrowed into Swahili, ﻖ (qaaf) was changed to /k/. For example: SWAADIQ ﺻﺎدﻖ became SADIKI, TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ became TARIKI, ‘AQLI عﻘل became AKILI, WARAQA ﻮﺭﻗﻪ became WARAKA, and WAQTI ﻮﻗﺖ became WAKATI.

Change of ﻇ (Dhwee) in Arabic to /Dh/ in Swahili

ﻇ (dhwee) is the seventeenth letter in the Arabic alphabet. When words containing this sound were borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, ﻇ (dhwee) was replaced by /dh/. For example: DHWAALIM ﺂلﻡﻇ became DHALIMU, and NADHWIIF نﻈﯿﻒ became NADHIFU.

Dropping of Arabic Vowels in Swahili

In some Arabic words, there is a prolonged sound or two vowels. When borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, one of the vowels is dropped, leaving only one. For example: TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ changed to become TARIKI, DHWAALIM ﻇﺂلﻡ changed to become DHALIMU, NADHWIIF نﻈﯿﻒ changed to become NADHIFU. Change of ﺽ ('Ddwad) from Arabic to /Dh/ in Swahili: ﺽ ('Ddwad) is the fifteenth consonant in the Arabic alphabet. Most experts classify this sound as /d/, but it is not /d/. It is a sound articulated with the front part of the tongue (not the tip) and the teeth. This sound poses a challenge to pronounce, especially for speakers who are not familiar with the Arabic language. The Swahili do not have this sound, so they looked for a similar one and found /dh/, and immediately words with ﺽ ('llwad) in Arabic changed and began to be pronounced with /dh/ after being incorporated into the Swahili language. An example is: AR'LLI ﺃﺮﺾ changes to become ARDHI; 'LLAR ABUROHD B n ﺮkn an k an ﺐﺮﺿDH. Change in /H/ That Is Voiced and /H/ That Is Unvoiced In the Arabic language, there are two types of /h/. The first is ﺡ /h/ unvoiced and is pronounced from the upper part of the throat. Then there is ﻫ /h/ that is voiced and is pronounced from the chest. In the Swahili language, there is only one /h/, which is pronounced in the throat. Those Arabic words containing the sound /h/ ﻫ that is voiced, when borrowed into the Swahili language, this sound is changed to an unvoiced /h/. for example: “AHDI عﻬد changed to become AHADI, JUHDI ﺠﻫد… The Dropping of Final Sounds in Arabic Words Some Arabic words have final sounds that are often used as suffixes at the end of the word and are usually ﺀ (hamza) and ﺓ /t/. for example: HAYAAI ﺤﻳﺎﺀ, the hamza is dropped and a vowel following /y/ is also removed, so the word changes to HAYA. SWADAQAATU ﺼدﻗﺎﺕ, the final /t/ is dropped and a vowel after /q/ is removed, /qaaf/ becomes /k/, and the word changes to SADAKA. RISAALATU ﺮﺴﺎلﺔ, the final /t/ is dropped and a vowel after /s/ is removed, so the word changes to RISALA. WARAQATU ﻮﺭﻗﺔ, the final /t/ is dropped and /qaaf/ becomes /k/, so the word changes to WARAKA. Transfer of Arabic Word Structures into Swahili: Swahili words are usually arranged in a CV-CV (consonant-vowel) structure. for example, KAKA, DADA, MAMA, etc. Most Arabic words, when borrowed, generally do not follow this pattern of the Swahili language. They usually have the structure CVCCV, etc. However, when they are borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, they are supplied with vowels and changed to follow the CV-CV structure. For example:
‘AHDI (CVCCV) عﻬد changed to become AHADI (VCVCV), JUHDI (CVCVCV) ﺠﻫد became JUHUDI (CVCVCVCV). However, there are some words that retained their Arabic structure when borrowed into Swahili, thereby introducing a new word structure into the Swahili language from Arabic. For example: AR’LLI ﺃﺮﺾ (VCCV) becomes ARDHI (VCCV), KHAMSIIN ﺨﻤﺴﯿﻦ (CVCVCCVC) — when this word was borrowed into Swahili, it retained its original Arabic structure, but underwent a few changes, namely, /kh/ changed to /h/, a vowel immediately after /s/ was dropped, and a vowel was added to the end of the word. But no vowel was inserted after /m/, so the Arabic structure was preserved as it entered Swahili and the word became HAMSINI (CVCVCVCV).

Changes in meaning for some of the borrowed Arabic words.
Most Arabic words borrowed and incorporated into Swahili retained their original meaning from Arabic. However, some words changed meaning after being borrowed and acquired new meanings in the Swahili language. This section will examine some words whose meanings changed following borrowing.

Dari is a Swahili word borrowed from Arabic ﺪﺍﺭ (dār). The original Arabic meaning of this word is HOUSE (NYUMBA), as seen in the phrase ﺪﺍﺭﺴﻼﻡ DĀR SALĀM meaning HOUSE OF PEACE. When borrowed into Swahili, however, its meaning changed—it no longer referred to a 'house' but rather to the upper part of a house, just below the roof.

Alhamisi is a Swahili word borrowed from the Arabic word ﺃﻠﺧﻤﻴﺱ (alkhamīs). According to the Arabic weekly calendar, Alkhamiis is the fifth day. But in Swahili, it is the sixth day of the week. Let us compare the days of the week in Arabic and Swahili:

Swahili               Arabic
Jumamosi (first day of the week)      ﻴﻮﻡﺍﻠﺴﺑﺖ (yaumu sabt)    the day of rest
Jumapili (second day of the week)     ﻳﻭﻢﺍﻷﺤﺪ (yaumul-ahad)  the first day of the week
Jumatatu (third day of the week)      ﻳﻭﻡﺍﻹﺜﻧﻴﻦ (yaumul-ithnayn)  the second day of the week
Jumanne (fourth day of the week)      ﻴﻭﻢﺍﻟﺜﻸﺘﺎﺀ (yaumu thulāthā')  the third day of the week
Jumatano (fifth day of the week)      ﺀﻭﻢﺍﻷﺮﺑﻌﺎﺀ (yaumul-arba'ā')   the fourth day of the week
Alhamisi (sixth day of the week)      ﺃﻠﺧﻤﻴﺱ (alkhamīs)      the fifth day of the week
Ijumaa (day of completing the week)   ﻴﻭﻢﺍﻟﺟﻤﻌﺔ (yaumul-jumu‘a)     the last day of the week

According to the comparison between Swahili and Arabic days, it is clear that the days do not align: the first day in Swahili (Jumamosi) in Arabic is the day of rest, and the second day in Swahili is the first day of the week in Arabic, and so forth. Swahili borrowed two words, ALHAMISI and IJUMAA, from Arabic. However, the word ALHAMISI—which meant ‘the fifth day’ in Arabic—when it entered the Swahili language, its meaning changed to ‘the sixth day of the week.’

Sakafu is a Swahili word borrowed from the Arabic ﺴﻘﻒ (saqf). In Arabic, saqf means CEILING, that is, the upper part of a house beneath the roof. However, when this word was borrowed into Swahili, its meaning changed to refer to the lower part of the house—that which is laid and cemented.

Nahau is another word borrowed from the Arabic ﺍﻟنﺤﻭ (an-nahwu), which originally means GRAMMAR in Arabic. However, when incorporated into Swahili, the word took on a new meaning: a group of words that together carry a special meaning not directly derived from the usual meanings of the individual words. Linguistics is a word that was also borrowed from the Arabic language ﺍﻹﺴﻡ (al-ismu), whose original meaning is NAME. When this word was borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, its meaning changed to refer to the discipline that studies and scientifically analyzes language. Waraka was also borrowed from the Arabic language ﻮﺭﻗﺔ (waraqatu). The original meaning of this word in Arabic is LEAF OF A TREE. However, when it was borrowed and incorporated into the Swahili language, its meaning changed to refer to documents written on a piece of paper that convey certain information. In conclusion, this article examines and analyzes the various phonological changes of Arabic words that were borrowed and incorporated into Swahili. After identifying various changes, it was determined that many Arabic words were adapted into Swahili after being borrowed, with their consonants altered to simplify pronunciation for Bantu speakers. In addition, there are sounds and pronunciation patterns that were borrowed directly from Arabic without any modification. Moreover, there were also changes in meaning in some of the borrowed Arabic words incorporated into the Swahili language. Therefore, the evidence shows that both changes in meaning and pronunciation occurred in some Swahili words borrowed from Arabic. References:- 1. Khamisi A. B. Utangulizi:- Wakati Kiswahili kilipokutana na lugha ya Kiarabu, kilikopa mambo mawili. Kilichukua maneno mengi ya Kiarabu na kuyabadilisha, na pili, kilichukua sauti za Kiarabu zilizokuja na baadhi ya maneno hayo. Uingizaji wa maneno na sauti za Kiarabu katika lugha ya Kiswahili ulisababisha aina mbili za mabadiliko ya lugha. Aina ya kwanza ya mabadiliko ni mabadiliko au urahisishaji wa sauti za Kiarabu ili ziweze kutamkwa na wasemaji wa Kiswahili, ambayo ni lugha ya Kibantu. Pili, kulikuwa na mabadiliko ya maana ya asili ya baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yalipopokelewa katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Makala haya yatajadili ukopaji wa lugha kutoka Kiarabu kuingia Kiswahili, njia ambazo mabadiliko ya sauti yalitokea, na mabadiliko ya maana ya asili ya baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yaliyokopwa katika Kiswahili. Makala haya yanatumia nadharia mbili. Ya kwanza ni nadharia ya muundo, inayoshughulikia mabadiliko ya sauti za maneno yaliyokopwa kutoka lugha ya Kiarabu. Kulingana na Mulder na Hervy (1975), nadharia hii inaangalia lugha kama mfumo mkubwa wenye mifumo midogo mingi ndani yake. Wanasema kwamba lugha ni mfumo wenye mifumo midogo mitano: semantiki, pragmatiki, sintaksia. Morfolojia na fonolojia. Makala hii itajikita kwenye fonolojia, ikichunguza jinsi sauti zinavyobadilika. Nadharia ya pili ni ile ya semantiki leksika ya kiutambuzi. Kwa mujibu wa Paradis (2012), nadharia hii inashughulikia mabadiliko ya maana katika maneno, ambayo ni mojawapo ya mada za makala hii. Hamisi Babusa. Anwani: Chuo Kikuu cha Kenyatta. Mabadiliko ya sauti katika maneno ya Kiarabu yaliyoazimwa. Maneno mengi ya Kiarabu yaliyoazimwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili, pamoja na kupitia mabadiliko ili kuendana na mifumo ya irabu na kufuata muundo wa maneno ya Kiswahili, pia yalipata mabadiliko ya sauti zake asilia. Sauti hizi zilibadilishwa kwa sababu hazikuwapo kabisa katika Kiswahili, na hata kama zingechukuliwa moja kwa moja, zingesababisha ugumu wa matamshi kwa wasemaji wa Kiswahili ambao hawakuwa na kawaida ya kutamka sauti hizo za Kiarabu. Mifano ifuatayo inaonyesha mabadiliko ya matamshi ya baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu ambayo yameingizwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Tofauti kati ya herufi ya Kiarabu ي (Yee) na irabu ya Kiswahili. Herufi ya Kiarabu ي (Yee) au /y/ ni konsonanti ya mwisho katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu. Kuna maneno fulani ya Kiarabu yenye (yee) iliyo na shadda. Kwa mfano, MANIYYI منێ, NABIYYI نبێ, HAYYU حێ, TWAYYIB ﻄﯿﺐ, na MAYYITU مێټ. Maneno haya yalipochukuliwa katika Kiswahili, herufi ي (yee) iliondolewa na kubadilishwa na irabu /i/. MANIYYI ikawa MANII, NABIYYI ikawa NABII. HAYYU ikawa HAI, TWAYYIB ikawa taib, MAYYITU ikawa MAITI, n.k.

Tofauti kati ya herufi ya Kiarabu ع (‘Ain) na Kiwakilishi wa Kisiwa

ﻉ (‘ain) ni konsonanti ya kumi na nane katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu. Baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yenye sauti hii ni: ‘Aib عﯿﺐ, Mu‘allim معلم, ‘Ahdi عﻬد, ‘aqli عﻘل, na tis'a ﺗﺴعﺔ. Maneno haya yalipoazimwa na kuingizwa katika Kiswahili, herufi ya Kiarabu ﻉ ‘ain, ambayo ni ngumu kwa Waafrika kuitamka, iliondolewa na kubadilishwa na irabu. Kwa mfano, ‘aib ikawa AIBU, mu’allim ikawa MWALIMU, ‘ahdi ikawa AHADI, ‘aqli ikawa AKILI, na tis’a ikawa TISA.

Mabadiliko ya ﻄ (Twee) ya Kiarabu kuwa /T/ katika Kiswahili

Mabadiliko mengine ya sauti hutokea pale neno la Kiarabu lenye konsonanti ﻄ (twee) linapobadilishwa kuwa /t/ baada ya kuazimwa katika Kiswahili. Kwa mfano, maneno yafuatayo yametoka katika Kiarabu: TWAYYIB ﻄﯿﺐ na TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ. Maneno haya yalipoazimwa na kuingizwa kwenye Kiswahili, konsonanti ﻂ (twee) iliondolewa na kubadilishwa na /t/, hivyo kupata maneno ya Kiswahili TARIKI na TAIB.

Mabadiliko ya ﺺ (Swaad) ya Kiarabu kuwa /S/ katika Kiswahili

Maneno ya Kiarabu yenye konsonanti ﺺ (swaad), yanapofika katika lugha ya Kiswahili, hubadilishwa na ﺺ (swaad) inakuwa /s/. Kwa mfano: SWAADIQ ﺻﺎدﻖ ilibadilika kuwa SADIKI, SWAGHYR ﺻﻐﯿﺭ ikawa SAGHIRI, na SWIRAAT ﺻﺮﺁﺖ ikawa SIRATI.

Mabadiliko ya ﻖ (Qaaf) ya Kiarabu kuwa /K/ katika Kiswahili

Katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu, kuna ﻙ (kaaf) /k/ na ﻖ (qaaf). ﻖ (qaaf) ni konsonanti ya ishirini na moja katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu, hutamkwa nyuma zaidi mdomoni kuliko /k/, yaani, kwa kugusana kwenye kaakaa laini na nyuma ya ulimi. Wasemaji wa Kibantu hawakuwa na sauti hii, na maneno yenye sauti hii ya Kiarabu yalipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, ﻖ (qaaf) ilibadilishwa kuwa /k/. Kwa mfano: SWAADIQ ﺻﺎدﻖ ilibadilika kuwa SADIKI, TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ ikawa TARIKI, ‘AQLI عﻘل ikawa AKILI, WARAQA ﻮﺭﻗﻪ ikawa WARAKA, na WAQTI ﻮﻗﺖ ikawa WAKATI.

Mabadiliko ya ﻇ (Dhwee) ya Kiarabu kuwa /Dh/ katika Kiswahili

ﻇ (dhwee) ni herufi ya kumi na saba katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu. Maneno yenye sauti hii yalipoazimwa na kuingizwa Kiswahili, ﻇ (dhwee) ilibadilishwa na kuwa /dh/. Kwa mfano: DHWAALIM ﺂلﻡﻇ ilibadilishwa kuwa DHALIMU, na NADHWIIF نﻈﯿﻒ ikawa NADHIFU.

Kuachwa kwa irabu za Kiarabu katika Kiswahili

Katika baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu, kuna sauti ndefu au irabu mbili. Zinapoazimwa na kuingizwa Kiswahili, irabu moja hutolewa, kubaki moja tu. Kwa mfano: TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ ilibadilishwa kuwa TARIKI, DHWAALIM ﻇﺂلﻡ ilibadilishwa kuwa DHALIMU, NADHWIIF نﻈﯿﻒ ilibadilishwa kuwa NADHIFU. Mabadiliko ya ﺽ ('Ddwad) kutoka Kiarabu hadi /Dh/ katika Kiswahili: ﺽ ('Ddwad) ni konsonanti ya kumi na tano katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu. Wataalamu wengi huiainisha sauti hii kama /d/, lakini si /d/. Ni sauti inayotamkwa kwa kutumia sehemu ya mbele ya ulimi (si ncha yake) na meno. Sauti hii inaleta changamoto ya kutamka, hasa kwa wasemaji ambao hawazoei lugha ya Kiarabu. Waswahili hawana sauti hii, hivyo walitafuta ile inayofanana na wakapata /dh/, na mara moja maneno yenye ﺽ ('llwad) kwa Kiarabu yalibadilika na kuanza kutamkwa kwa /dh/ baada ya kuingizwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Mfano ni: AR'LLI ﺃﺮﺾ hubadilika kuwa ARDHI; 'LLAR ABUROHD B n ﺮkn an k an ﺐﺮﺿDH. Mabadiliko katika /H/ Ambayo Ina Sauti na /H/ Ambayo Haina Sauti Katika lugha ya Kiarabu, kuna aina mbili za /h/. Ya kwanza ni ﺡ /h/ isiyo na sauti na inatamkwa kutoka sehemu ya juu ya koo. Halafu kuna ﻫ /h/ yenye sauti na inatamkwa kutoka kifuani. Katika lugha ya Kiswahili, kuna /h/ moja tu, ambayo hutamkwa kooni. Maneno ya Kiarabu yenye sauti /h/ ﻫ ambayo ni yenye sauti, yanapoazimwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili, sauti hii hubadilika kuwa /h/ isiyo na sauti. kwa mfano: “AHDI عﻬد ilibadilika kuwa AHADI, JUHDI ﺠﻫد… Kuachwa kwa Sauti za Mwisho katika Maneno ya Kiarabu Baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yana sauti za mwisho ambazo mara nyingi hutumiwa kama viambishi tamati mwisho wa neno na kwa kawaida ni ﺀ (hamza) na ﺓ /t/.” Kwa mfano: HAYAAI ﺤﻳﺎﺀ, hamza inaondolewa na irabu inayofuata /y/ pia inaondolewa, hivyo neno linabadilika kuwa HAYA. SWADAQAATU ﺼدﻗﺎﺕ, /t/ ya mwisho inaondolewa na irabu baada ya /q/ inaondolewa, /qaaf/ inakuwa /k/, na neno linakuwa SADAKA. RISAALATU ﺮﺴﺎلﺔ, /t/ ya mwisho inaondolewa na irabu baada ya /s/ inaondolewa, hivyo neno linakuwa RISALA. WARAQATU ﻮﺭﻗﺔ, /t/ ya mwisho inaondolewa na /qaaf/ inakuwa /k/, hivyo neno linakuwa WARAKA. Uhamisho wa Miundo ya Maneno ya Kiarabu katika Kiswahili: Maneno ya Kiswahili mara nyingi hupangwa katika muundo wa silabi za K-V (konsonanti-irabu). kwa mfano, KAKA, DADA, MAMA, n.k. Maneno mengi ya Kiarabu, yanapokopwa, kwa ujumla hayafwati mtindo huu wa lugha ya Kiswahili. Kwa kawaida huwa na muundo wa CVCCV, n.k. Hata hivyo, zinapokopwa na kuingizwa katika Kiswahili, huongezewa vokali na kubadilishwa ili kufuata muundo wa CV-CV. Kwa mfano:
'AHDI (CVCCV) عﻬد ilibadilika kuwa AHADI (VCVCV), JUHDI (CVCVCV) ﺠﻫد ikawa JUHUDI (CVCVCVCV). Hata hivyo, kuna maneno mengine yaliyobaki na muundo wake wa Kiarabu yalipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, hivyo kuanzisha muundo mpya wa neno katika Kiswahili kutoka Kiarabu. Kwa mfano: AR’LLI ﺃﺮﺾ (VCCV) inakuwa ARDHI (VCCV), KHAMSIIN ﺨﻤﺴﯿﻦ (CVCVCCVC) — neno hili lilipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, lilibaki na muundo wake wa Kiarabu, lakini likapata mabadiliko kadhaa, yaani, /kh/ ilibadilika kuwa /h/, irabu iliyokuwa mara moja baada ya /s/ iliondolewa, na irabu ikaongezwa mwishoni mwa neno. Lakini hakuna irabu iliyoingizwa baada ya /m/, hivyo muundo wa Kiarabu ulihifadhiwa lilipoingia Kiswahili na neno likawa HAMSINI (CVCVCVCV).

Mabadiliko ya maana kwa baadhi ya maneno yaliyokopwa kutoka Kiarabu.
Maneno mengi ya Kiarabu yaliyoazimwa na kuingizwa Kiswahili yamehifadhi maana yake ya awali kutoka Kiarabu. Hata hivyo, baadhi ya maneno yalibadilika maana baada ya kuazimwa na kupata maana mpya katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Sehemu hii itachunguza baadhi ya maneno ambayo maana yake ilibadilika baada ya kuazimwa.

Dari ni neno la Kiswahili lililoazimwa kutoka Kiarabu ﺪﺍﺭ (dār). Maana ya awali ya Kiarabu ya neno hili ni NYUMBA, kama inavyoonekana katika msemo ﺪﺍﺭﺴﻼﻡ DĀR SALĀM maana yake NYUMBA YA AMANI. Hata hivyo, lilipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika—halikurejelea tena 'nyumba' bali sehemu ya juu ya nyumba, chini ya paa.

Alhamisi ni neno la Kiswahili lililoazimwa kutoka kwenye neno la Kiarabu ﺃﻠﺧﻤﻴﺱ (alkhamīs). Kwa mujibu wa kalenda ya wiki ya Kiarabu, Alkhamiis ni siku ya tano. Lakini katika Kiswahili, ni siku ya sita ya wiki. Tuchunguze kulinganisha siku za wiki katika Kiarabu na Kiswahili:

Kiswahili                  Kiarabu
Jumamosi (siku ya kwanza ya wiki)             ﻴﻮﻡﺍﻠﺴﺑﺖ (yaumu sabt)         siku ya mapumziko
Jumapili (siku ya pili ya wiki)                ﻳﻭﻢﺍﻷﺤﺪ (yaumul-ahad)       siku ya kwanza ya wiki
Jumatatu (siku ya tatu ya wiki)               ﻳﻭﻡﺍﻹﺜﻧﻴﻦ (yaumul-ithnayn)      siku ya pili ya wiki
Jumanne (siku ya nne ya wiki)                 ﻴﻭﻢﺍﻟﺜﻸﺘﺎﺀ (yaumu thulāthā')    siku ya tatu ya wiki
Jumatano (siku ya tano ya wiki)               ﺀﻭﻢﺍﻷﺮﺑﻌﺎﺀ (yaumul-arba'ā')     siku ya nne ya wiki
Alhamisi (siku ya sita ya wiki)               ﺃﻠﺧﻤﻴﺱ (alkhamīs)           siku ya tano ya wiki
Ijumaa (siku ya kukamilisha wiki)             ﻴﻭﻢﺍﻟﺟﻤﻌﺔ (yaumul-jumu‘a)         siku ya mwisho wa wiki

Kwa mujibu wa ulinganisho wa siku za Kiswahili na Kiarabu, ni wazi kuwa siku hazilingani: siku ya kwanza ya Kiswahili (Jumamosi) katika Kiarabu ni siku ya mapumziko, na siku ya pili ya Kiswahili ndiyo siku ya kwanza ya wiki katika Kiarabu, na kadhalika. Kiswahili kiliazima maneno mawili, ALHAMISI na IJUMAA, kutoka Kiarabu. Hata hivyo, neno ALHAMISI—ambalo lilimaanisha 'siku ya tano' kwa Kiarabu—lilipoingia katika lugha ya Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika kuwa ‘siku ya sita ya wiki.’

Sakafu ni neno la Kiswahili lililoazimwa kutoka Kiarabu ﺴﻘﻒ (saqf). Kwa Kiarabu, saqf maana yake ni DARI, yaani, sehemu ya juu ya nyumba chini ya paa. Hata hivyo, neno hili lilipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika na kurejelea sehemu ya chini ya nyumba—ile iliyowekwa na kupigwa simenti.

Nahau ni neno jingine lililoazimwa kutoka Kiarabu ﺍﻟنﺤﻭ (an-nahwu), ambalo asili yake maana yake ni SARUFI kwa Kiarabu. Hata hivyo, lilipoingizwa katika Kiswahili, neno hili lilipata maana mpya: kundi la maneno ambalo linapounganishwa linakuwa na maana maalum isiyotokana moja kwa moja na maana za kawaida za maneno hayo. Isimu ni neno ambalo pia lilichukuliwa kutoka katika lugha ya Kiarabu ﺍﻹﺴﻡ (al-ismu), ambalo maana yake asili ni JINA. Neno hili lilipochukuliwa na kuingizwa katika Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika na sasa linarejelea taaluma inayochunguza na kuchambua lugha kitaalamu. Neno waraka pia limeazimwa kutoka katika lugha ya Kiarabu ﻮﺭﻗﺔ (waraqatu). Maana ya awali ya neno hili katika Kiarabu ni JANI LA MTI. Hata hivyo, ilipokopwa na kuingizwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika kurejelea nyaraka zilizoandikwa kwenye kipande cha karatasi zinazowasilisha taarifa fulani. Kwa kumalizia, makala hii inachunguza na kuchambua mabadiliko mbalimbali ya kifonolojia ya maneno ya Kiarabu yaliyokopwa na kuingizwa katika Kiswahili. Baada ya kubaini mabadiliko mbalimbali, ilibainika kwamba maneno mengi ya Kiarabu yalichukuliwa na kubadilishwa katika Kiswahili baada ya kukopwa, huku konsonanti zao zikibadilishwa ili kurahisisha matamshi kwa wasemaji wa Kibantu. Zaidi ya hayo, kuna sauti na mifumo ya matamshi ambayo ilikopwa moja kwa moja kutoka Kiarabu bila mabadiliko yoyote. Aidha, kulikuwa pia na mabadiliko ya maana kwa baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yaliyokopwa na kuingizwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Hivyo basi, ushahidi unaonyesha kwamba mabadiliko ya maana na matamshi yalitokea kwa baadhi ya maneno ya Kiswahili yaliyokopwa kutoka Kiarabu. Marejeleo:- 1. Khamisi A. B. discourses.source_txt: When the Arabs arrived on the East African coast, they encountered the Swahili, and it was then that Swahili borrowed words and sounds from Arabic that did not previously exist in the Swahili language. Secondly, Swahili also adopted some Arabic sounds and modified the way they are pronounced. This article investigates and identifies the etymology of certain Arabic words found in the Swahili language and examines how Arabic sounds were borrowed, altered, and adapted into Swahili. Furthermore, it explores how the original meanings of some words changed after being borrowed from Arabic.

discourses.source_txt: …………………………………………………………………………………………………….... Introduction:- When Swahili came into contact with the Arabic language, it borrowed two things. It borrowed many Arabic words and adapted them, and secondly, it borrowed Arabic sounds that came with some of those words. The entry of Arabic words and sounds into the Swahili language resulted in two types of language change. The first type of change is the transformation or simplification of Arabic sounds so they can be pronounced by speakers of Swahili, which is a Bantu language. Secondly, there was a change in the original meaning of some Arabic words when they were incorporated into the Swahili language. This article will discuss language borrowing from Arabic into Swahili, the ways in which sound changes took place, and the alteration of the original meaning of some Arabic words borrowed into Swahili. This article employs two theories. The first is the structural theory, which deals with the changes in the sounds of words borrowed from the Arabic language. According to Mulder and Hervy (1975), this theory regards language as a large system comprised of many subsystems within it. They state that language is a system with five subsystems: semantics, pragmatics, syntax.
discourses.translated_txt: Utangulizi:- Wakati Kiswahili kilipokutana na lugha ya Kiarabu, kilikopa mambo mawili. Kilichukua maneno mengi ya Kiarabu na kuyabadilisha, na pili, kilichukua sauti za Kiarabu zilizokuja na baadhi ya maneno hayo. Uingizaji wa maneno na sauti za Kiarabu katika lugha ya Kiswahili ulisababisha aina mbili za mabadiliko ya lugha. Aina ya kwanza ya mabadiliko ni mabadiliko au urahisishaji wa sauti za Kiarabu ili ziweze kutamkwa na wasemaji wa Kiswahili, ambayo ni lugha ya Kibantu. Pili, kulikuwa na mabadiliko ya maana ya asili ya baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yalipopokelewa katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Makala haya yatajadili ukopaji wa lugha kutoka Kiarabu kuingia Kiswahili, njia ambazo mabadiliko ya sauti yalitokea, na mabadiliko ya maana ya asili ya baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yaliyokopwa katika Kiswahili. Makala haya yanatumia nadharia mbili. Ya kwanza ni nadharia ya muundo, inayoshughulikia mabadiliko ya sauti za maneno yaliyokopwa kutoka lugha ya Kiarabu. Kulingana na Mulder na Hervy (1975), nadharia hii inaangalia lugha kama mfumo mkubwa wenye mifumo midogo mingi ndani yake. Wanasema kwamba lugha ni mfumo wenye mifumo midogo mitano: semantiki, pragmatiki, sintaksia.

HAYYU became HAI, TWAYYIB became taib, MAYYITU became MAITI, etc.

Differentiation of the Arabic ع (‘Ain) and the Swahili Vowel

ﻉ (‘ain) is the eighteenth consonant in the Arabic alphabet. Some Arabic words that contain this sound include: ‘Aib عﯿﺐ, Mu‘allim معلم, ‘Ahdi عﻬد, ‘aqli عﻘل, and tis'a ﺗﺴعﺔ. When these words were borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, the Arabic ﻉ ‘ain, which is difficult for Africans to pronounce, was dropped and replaced with a vowel. For example, ‘aib became AIBU, mu’allim became MWALIMU, ‘ahdi became AHADI, ‘aqli became AKILI, and tis’a became TISA.

Change of ﻄ (Twee) in Arabic to /T/ in Swahili

Another sound change occurs where an Arabic word containing the ﻄ (twee) consonant is changed to /t/ after being borrowed into Swahili. For example, the following words are from Arabic: TWAYYIB ﻄﯿﺐ and TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ. When these words were borrowed and incorporated into the Swahili language, the ﻂ (twee) consonant was dropped and replaced with /t/, resulting in the Swahili words TARIKI and TAIB.

Change of ﺺ (Swaad) in Arabic to /S/ in Swahili

Arabic words that have the ﺺ (swaad) consonant, when entering the Swahili language, are changed so that ﺺ (swaad) becomes /s/. For example: SWAADIQ ﺻﺎدﻖ changed to SADIKI, SWAGHYR ﺻﻐﯿﺭ changed to SAGHIRI, and SWIRAAT ﺻﺮﺁﺖ changed to SIRATI.

Change of ﻖ (Qaaf) in Arabic to /K/ in Swahili

In the Arabic alphabet, there is ﻙ (kaaf) /k/ and ﻖ (qaaf). ﻖ (qaaf) is the twenty-first consonant in the Arabic alphabet, pronounced further back in the mouth than /k/, i.e., with contact at the soft palate and the back of the tongue. Bantu speakers did not have this sound, and when words with this Arabic sound were borrowed into Swahili, ﻖ (qaaf) was changed to /k/. For example: SWAADIQ ﺻﺎدﻖ became SADIKI, TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ became TARIKI, ‘AQLI عﻘل became AKILI, WARAQA ﻮﺭﻗﻪ became WARAKA, and WAQTI ﻮﻗﺖ became WAKATI.

Change of ﻇ (Dhwee) in Arabic to /Dh/ in Swahili

ﻇ (dhwee) is the seventeenth letter in the Arabic alphabet. When words containing this sound were borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, ﻇ (dhwee) was replaced by /dh/. For example: DHWAALIM ﺂلﻡﻇ became DHALIMU, and NADHWIIF نﻈﯿﻒ became NADHIFU.

Dropping of Arabic Vowels in Swahili

In some Arabic words, there is a prolonged sound or two vowels. When borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, one of the vowels is dropped, leaving only one.

HAYYU ikawa HAI, TWAYYIB ikawa taib, MAYYITU ikawa MAITI, n.k.

Tofauti kati ya herufi ya Kiarabu ع (‘Ain) na Kiwakilishi wa Kisiwa

ﻉ (‘ain) ni konsonanti ya kumi na nane katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu. Baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yenye sauti hii ni: ‘Aib عﯿﺐ, Mu‘allim معلم, ‘Ahdi عﻬد, ‘aqli عﻘل, na tis'a ﺗﺴعﺔ. Maneno haya yalipoazimwa na kuingizwa katika Kiswahili, herufi ya Kiarabu ﻉ ‘ain, ambayo ni ngumu kwa Waafrika kuitamka, iliondolewa na kubadilishwa na irabu. Kwa mfano, ‘aib ikawa AIBU, mu’allim ikawa MWALIMU, ‘ahdi ikawa AHADI, ‘aqli ikawa AKILI, na tis’a ikawa TISA.

Mabadiliko ya ﻄ (Twee) ya Kiarabu kuwa /T/ katika Kiswahili

Mabadiliko mengine ya sauti hutokea pale neno la Kiarabu lenye konsonanti ﻄ (twee) linapobadilishwa kuwa /t/ baada ya kuazimwa katika Kiswahili. Kwa mfano, maneno yafuatayo yametoka katika Kiarabu: TWAYYIB ﻄﯿﺐ na TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ. Maneno haya yalipoazimwa na kuingizwa kwenye Kiswahili, konsonanti ﻂ (twee) iliondolewa na kubadilishwa na /t/, hivyo kupata maneno ya Kiswahili TARIKI na TAIB.

Mabadiliko ya ﺺ (Swaad) ya Kiarabu kuwa /S/ katika Kiswahili

Maneno ya Kiarabu yenye konsonanti ﺺ (swaad), yanapofika katika lugha ya Kiswahili, hubadilishwa na ﺺ (swaad) inakuwa /s/. Kwa mfano: SWAADIQ ﺻﺎدﻖ ilibadilika kuwa SADIKI, SWAGHYR ﺻﻐﯿﺭ ikawa SAGHIRI, na SWIRAAT ﺻﺮﺁﺖ ikawa SIRATI.

Mabadiliko ya ﻖ (Qaaf) ya Kiarabu kuwa /K/ katika Kiswahili

Katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu, kuna ﻙ (kaaf) /k/ na ﻖ (qaaf). ﻖ (qaaf) ni konsonanti ya ishirini na moja katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu, hutamkwa nyuma zaidi mdomoni kuliko /k/, yaani, kwa kugusana kwenye kaakaa laini na nyuma ya ulimi. Wasemaji wa Kibantu hawakuwa na sauti hii, na maneno yenye sauti hii ya Kiarabu yalipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, ﻖ (qaaf) ilibadilishwa kuwa /k/. Kwa mfano: SWAADIQ ﺻﺎدﻖ ilibadilika kuwa SADIKI, TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ ikawa TARIKI, ‘AQLI عﻘل ikawa AKILI, WARAQA ﻮﺭﻗﻪ ikawa WARAKA, na WAQTI ﻮﻗﺖ ikawa WAKATI.

Mabadiliko ya ﻇ (Dhwee) ya Kiarabu kuwa /Dh/ katika Kiswahili

ﻇ (dhwee) ni herufi ya kumi na saba katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu. Maneno yenye sauti hii yalipoazimwa na kuingizwa Kiswahili, ﻇ (dhwee) ilibadilishwa na kuwa /dh/. Kwa mfano: DHWAALIM ﺂلﻡﻇ ilibadilishwa kuwa DHALIMU, na NADHWIIF نﻈﯿﻒ ikawa NADHIFU.

Kuachwa kwa irabu za Kiarabu katika Kiswahili

Katika baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu, kuna sauti ndefu au irabu mbili. Zinapoazimwa na kuingizwa Kiswahili, irabu moja hutolewa, kubaki moja tu.

discourses.source_txt: For example: TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ changed to become TARIKI, DHWAALIM ﻇﺂلﻡ changed to become DHALIMU, NADHWIIF نﻈﯿﻒ changed to become NADHIFU. Change of ﺽ ('Ddwad) from Arabic to /Dh/ in Swahili: ﺽ ('Ddwad) is the fifteenth consonant in the Arabic alphabet.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa mfano: TWAARIQ ﻄﺂﺮﻖ ilibadilishwa kuwa TARIKI, DHWAALIM ﻇﺂلﻡ ilibadilishwa kuwa DHALIMU, NADHWIIF نﻈﯿﻒ ilibadilishwa kuwa NADHIFU. Mabadiliko ya ﺽ ('Ddwad) kutoka Kiarabu hadi /Dh/ katika Kiswahili: ﺽ ('Ddwad) ni konsonanti ya kumi na tano katika alfabeti ya Kiarabu.

discourses.source_txt: Most experts classify this sound as /d/, but it is not /d/.
discourses.translated_txt: Wataalamu wengi huiainisha sauti hii kama /d/, lakini si /d/.

discourses.source_txt: It is a sound articulated with the front part of the tongue (not the tip) and the teeth. This sound poses a challenge to pronounce, especially for speakers who are not familiar with the Arabic language.
discourses.translated_txt: Ni sauti inayotamkwa kwa kutumia sehemu ya mbele ya ulimi (si ncha yake) na meno. Sauti hii inaleta changamoto ya kutamka, hasa kwa wasemaji ambao hawazoei lugha ya Kiarabu.

discourses.source_txt: The Swahili do not have this sound, so they looked for a similar one and found /dh/, and immediately words with ﺽ ('llwad) in Arabic changed and began to be pronounced with /dh/ after being incorporated into the Swahili language.
discourses.translated_txt: Waswahili hawana sauti hii, hivyo walitafuta ile inayofanana na wakapata /dh/, na mara moja maneno yenye ﺽ ('llwad) kwa Kiarabu yalibadilika na kuanza kutamkwa kwa /dh/ baada ya kuingizwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili.

discourses.source_txt: An example is: AR'LLI ﺃﺮﺾ changes to become ARDHI; 'LLAR ABUROHD B n ﺮkn an k an ﺐﺮﺿDH. Change in /H/ That Is Voiced and /H/ That Is Unvoiced In the Arabic language, there are two types of /h/. The first is ﺡ /h/ unvoiced and is pronounced from the upper part of the throat. Then there is ﻫ /h/ that is voiced and is pronounced from the chest.
discourses.translated_txt: Mfano ni: AR'LLI ﺃﺮﺾ hubadilika kuwa ARDHI; 'LLAR ABUROHD B n ﺮkn an k an ﺐﺮﺿDH. Mabadiliko katika /H/ Ambayo Ina Sauti na /H/ Ambayo Haina Sauti Katika lugha ya Kiarabu, kuna aina mbili za /h/. Ya kwanza ni ﺡ /h/ isiyo na sauti na inatamkwa kutoka sehemu ya juu ya koo. Halafu kuna ﻫ /h/ yenye sauti na inatamkwa kutoka kifuani.

discourses.source_txt: In the Swahili language, there is only one /h/, which is pronounced in the throat.
discourses.translated_txt: Katika lugha ya Kiswahili, kuna /h/ moja tu, ambayo hutamkwa kooni.

discourses.source_txt: Those Arabic words containing the sound /h/ ﻫ that is voiced, when borrowed into the Swahili language, this sound is changed to an unvoiced /h/.
discourses.translated_txt: Maneno ya Kiarabu yenye sauti /h/ ﻫ ambayo ni yenye sauti, yanapoazimwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili, sauti hii hubadilika kuwa /h/ isiyo na sauti.

discourses.source_txt: for example: “AHDI عﻬد changed to become AHADI, JUHDI ﺠﻫد… The Dropping of Final Sounds in Arabic Words Some Arabic words have final sounds that are often used as suffixes at the end of the word and are usually ﺀ (hamza) and ﺓ /t/.
discourses.translated_txt: kwa mfano: “AHDI عﻬد ilibadilika kuwa AHADI, JUHDI ﺠﻫد… Kuachwa kwa Sauti za Mwisho katika Maneno ya Kiarabu Baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yana sauti za mwisho ambazo mara nyingi hutumiwa kama viambishi tamati mwisho wa neno na kwa kawaida ni ﺀ (hamza) na ﺓ /t/.”

discourses.source_txt: for example: HAYAAI ﺤﻳﺎﺀ, the hamza is dropped and a vowel following /y/ is also removed, so the word changes to HAYA. SWADAQAATU ﺼدﻗﺎﺕ, the final /t/ is dropped and a vowel after /q/ is removed, /qaaf/ becomes /k/, and the word changes to SADAKA. RISAALATU ﺮﺴﺎلﺔ, the final /t/ is dropped and a vowel after /s/ is removed, so the word changes to RISALA. WARAQATU ﻮﺭﻗﺔ, the final /t/ is dropped and /qaaf/ becomes /k/, so the word changes to WARAKA. Transfer of Arabic Word Structures into Swahili: Swahili words are usually arranged in a CV-CV (consonant-vowel) structure.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa mfano: HAYAAI ﺤﻳﺎﺀ, hamza inaondolewa na irabu inayofuata /y/ pia inaondolewa, hivyo neno linabadilika kuwa HAYA. SWADAQAATU ﺼدﻗﺎﺕ, /t/ ya mwisho inaondolewa na irabu baada ya /q/ inaondolewa, /qaaf/ inakuwa /k/, na neno linakuwa SADAKA. RISAALATU ﺮﺴﺎلﺔ, /t/ ya mwisho inaondolewa na irabu baada ya /s/ inaondolewa, hivyo neno linakuwa RISALA. WARAQATU ﻮﺭﻗﺔ, /t/ ya mwisho inaondolewa na /qaaf/ inakuwa /k/, hivyo neno linakuwa WARAKA. Uhamisho wa Miundo ya Maneno ya Kiarabu katika Kiswahili: Maneno ya Kiswahili mara nyingi hupangwa katika muundo wa silabi za K-V (konsonanti-irabu).

discourses.source_txt: for example, KAKA, DADA, MAMA, etc.
discourses.translated_txt: kwa mfano, KAKA, DADA, MAMA, n.k.

discourses.source_txt: Most Arabic words, when borrowed, generally do not follow this pattern of the Swahili language.
discourses.translated_txt: Maneno mengi ya Kiarabu, yanapokopwa, kwa ujumla hayafwati mtindo huu wa lugha ya Kiswahili.

discourses.source_txt: They usually have the structure CVCCV, etc. However, when they are borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, they are supplied with vowels and changed to follow the CV-CV structure.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa kawaida huwa na muundo wa CVCCV, n.k. Hata hivyo, zinapokopwa na kuingizwa katika Kiswahili, huongezewa vokali na kubadilishwa ili kufuata muundo wa CV-CV.

discourses.source_txt:
For example:
‘AHDI (CVCCV) عﻬد changed to become AHADI (VCVCV), JUHDI (CVCVCV) ﺠﻫد became JUHUDI (CVCVCVCV). However, there are some words that retained their Arabic structure when borrowed into Swahili, thereby introducing a new word structure into the Swahili language from Arabic. For example: AR’LLI ﺃﺮﺾ (VCCV) becomes ARDHI (VCCV), KHAMSIIN ﺨﻤﺴﯿﻦ (CVCVCCVC) — when this word was borrowed into Swahili, it retained its original Arabic structure, but underwent a few changes, namely, /kh/ changed to /h/, a vowel immediately after /s/ was dropped, and a vowel was added to the end of the word. But no vowel was inserted after /m/, so the Arabic structure was preserved as it entered Swahili and the word became HAMSINI (CVCVCVCV).

Changes in meaning for some of the borrowed Arabic words.
Most Arabic words borrowed and incorporated into Swahili retained their original meaning from Arabic. However, some words changed meaning after being borrowed and acquired new meanings in the Swahili language. This section will examine some words whose meanings changed following borrowing.

Dari is a Swahili word borrowed from Arabic ﺪﺍﺭ (dār). The original Arabic meaning of this word is HOUSE (NYUMBA), as seen in the phrase ﺪﺍﺭﺴﻼﻡ DĀR SALĀM meaning HOUSE OF PEACE. When borrowed into Swahili, however, its meaning changed—it no longer referred to a 'house' but rather to the upper part of a house, just below the roof.

Alhamisi is a Swahili word borrowed from the Arabic word ﺃﻠﺧﻤﻴﺱ (alkhamīs). According to the Arabic weekly calendar, Alkhamiis is the fifth day. But in Swahili, it is the sixth day of the week. Let us compare the days of the week in Arabic and Swahili:

Swahili               Arabic
Jumamosi (first day of the week)      ﻴﻮﻡﺍﻠﺴﺑﺖ (yaumu sabt)    the day of rest
Jumapili (second day of the week)     ﻳﻭﻢﺍﻷﺤﺪ (yaumul-ahad)  the first day of the week
Jumatatu (third day of the week)      ﻳﻭﻡﺍﻹﺜﻧﻴﻦ (yaumul-ithnayn)  the second day of the week
Jumanne (fourth day of the week)      ﻴﻭﻢﺍﻟﺜﻸﺘﺎﺀ (yaumu thulāthā')  the third day of the week
Jumatano (fifth day of the week)      ﺀﻭﻢﺍﻷﺮﺑﻌﺎﺀ (yaumul-arba'ā')   the fourth day of the week
Alhamisi (sixth day of the week)      ﺃﻠﺧﻤﻴﺱ (alkhamīs)      the fifth day of the week
Ijumaa (day of completing the week)   ﻴﻭﻢﺍﻟﺟﻤﻌﺔ (yaumul-jumu‘a)     the last day of the week

According to the comparison between Swahili and Arabic days, it is clear that the days do not align: the first day in Swahili (Jumamosi) in Arabic is the day of rest, and the second day in Swahili is the first day of the week in Arabic, and so forth. Swahili borrowed two words, ALHAMISI and IJUMAA, from Arabic. However, the word ALHAMISI—which meant ‘the fifth day’ in Arabic—when it entered the Swahili language, its meaning changed to ‘the sixth day of the week.’

Sakafu is a Swahili word borrowed from the Arabic ﺴﻘﻒ (saqf). In Arabic, saqf means CEILING, that is, the upper part of a house beneath the roof. However, when this word was borrowed into Swahili, its meaning changed to refer to the lower part of the house—that which is laid and cemented.

Nahau is another word borrowed from the Arabic ﺍﻟنﺤﻭ (an-nahwu), which originally means GRAMMAR in Arabic. However, when incorporated into Swahili, the word took on a new meaning: a group of words that together carry a special meaning not directly derived from the usual meanings of the individual words.
discourses.translated_txt:
Kwa mfano:
'AHDI (CVCCV) عﻬد ilibadilika kuwa AHADI (VCVCV), JUHDI (CVCVCV) ﺠﻫد ikawa JUHUDI (CVCVCVCV). Hata hivyo, kuna maneno mengine yaliyobaki na muundo wake wa Kiarabu yalipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, hivyo kuanzisha muundo mpya wa neno katika Kiswahili kutoka Kiarabu. Kwa mfano: AR’LLI ﺃﺮﺾ (VCCV) inakuwa ARDHI (VCCV), KHAMSIIN ﺨﻤﺴﯿﻦ (CVCVCCVC) — neno hili lilipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, lilibaki na muundo wake wa Kiarabu, lakini likapata mabadiliko kadhaa, yaani, /kh/ ilibadilika kuwa /h/, irabu iliyokuwa mara moja baada ya /s/ iliondolewa, na irabu ikaongezwa mwishoni mwa neno. Lakini hakuna irabu iliyoingizwa baada ya /m/, hivyo muundo wa Kiarabu ulihifadhiwa lilipoingia Kiswahili na neno likawa HAMSINI (CVCVCVCV).

Mabadiliko ya maana kwa baadhi ya maneno yaliyokopwa kutoka Kiarabu.
Maneno mengi ya Kiarabu yaliyoazimwa na kuingizwa Kiswahili yamehifadhi maana yake ya awali kutoka Kiarabu. Hata hivyo, baadhi ya maneno yalibadilika maana baada ya kuazimwa na kupata maana mpya katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Sehemu hii itachunguza baadhi ya maneno ambayo maana yake ilibadilika baada ya kuazimwa.

Dari ni neno la Kiswahili lililoazimwa kutoka Kiarabu ﺪﺍﺭ (dār). Maana ya awali ya Kiarabu ya neno hili ni NYUMBA, kama inavyoonekana katika msemo ﺪﺍﺭﺴﻼﻡ DĀR SALĀM maana yake NYUMBA YA AMANI. Hata hivyo, lilipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika—halikurejelea tena 'nyumba' bali sehemu ya juu ya nyumba, chini ya paa.

Alhamisi ni neno la Kiswahili lililoazimwa kutoka kwenye neno la Kiarabu ﺃﻠﺧﻤﻴﺱ (alkhamīs). Kwa mujibu wa kalenda ya wiki ya Kiarabu, Alkhamiis ni siku ya tano. Lakini katika Kiswahili, ni siku ya sita ya wiki. Tuchunguze kulinganisha siku za wiki katika Kiarabu na Kiswahili:

Kiswahili                  Kiarabu
Jumamosi (siku ya kwanza ya wiki)             ﻴﻮﻡﺍﻠﺴﺑﺖ (yaumu sabt)         siku ya mapumziko
Jumapili (siku ya pili ya wiki)                ﻳﻭﻢﺍﻷﺤﺪ (yaumul-ahad)       siku ya kwanza ya wiki
Jumatatu (siku ya tatu ya wiki)               ﻳﻭﻡﺍﻹﺜﻧﻴﻦ (yaumul-ithnayn)      siku ya pili ya wiki
Jumanne (siku ya nne ya wiki)                 ﻴﻭﻢﺍﻟﺜﻸﺘﺎﺀ (yaumu thulāthā')    siku ya tatu ya wiki
Jumatano (siku ya tano ya wiki)               ﺀﻭﻢﺍﻷﺮﺑﻌﺎﺀ (yaumul-arba'ā')     siku ya nne ya wiki
Alhamisi (siku ya sita ya wiki)               ﺃﻠﺧﻤﻴﺱ (alkhamīs)           siku ya tano ya wiki
Ijumaa (siku ya kukamilisha wiki)             ﻴﻭﻢﺍﻟﺟﻤﻌﺔ (yaumul-jumu‘a)         siku ya mwisho wa wiki

Kwa mujibu wa ulinganisho wa siku za Kiswahili na Kiarabu, ni wazi kuwa siku hazilingani: siku ya kwanza ya Kiswahili (Jumamosi) katika Kiarabu ni siku ya mapumziko, na siku ya pili ya Kiswahili ndiyo siku ya kwanza ya wiki katika Kiarabu, na kadhalika. Kiswahili kiliazima maneno mawili, ALHAMISI na IJUMAA, kutoka Kiarabu. Hata hivyo, neno ALHAMISI—ambalo lilimaanisha 'siku ya tano' kwa Kiarabu—lilipoingia katika lugha ya Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika kuwa ‘siku ya sita ya wiki.’

Sakafu ni neno la Kiswahili lililoazimwa kutoka Kiarabu ﺴﻘﻒ (saqf). Kwa Kiarabu, saqf maana yake ni DARI, yaani, sehemu ya juu ya nyumba chini ya paa. Hata hivyo, neno hili lilipoazimwa katika Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika na kurejelea sehemu ya chini ya nyumba—ile iliyowekwa na kupigwa simenti.

Nahau ni neno jingine lililoazimwa kutoka Kiarabu ﺍﻟنﺤﻭ (an-nahwu), ambalo asili yake maana yake ni SARUFI kwa Kiarabu. Hata hivyo, lilipoingizwa katika Kiswahili, neno hili lilipata maana mpya: kundi la maneno ambalo linapounganishwa linakuwa na maana maalum isiyotokana moja kwa moja na maana za kawaida za maneno hayo.

discourses.source_txt: Linguistics is a word that was also borrowed from the Arabic language ﺍﻹﺴﻡ (al-ismu), whose original meaning is NAME. When this word was borrowed and incorporated into Swahili, its meaning changed to refer to the discipline that studies and scientifically analyzes language.
discourses.translated_txt: Isimu ni neno ambalo pia lilichukuliwa kutoka katika lugha ya Kiarabu ﺍﻹﺴﻡ (al-ismu), ambalo maana yake asili ni JINA. Neno hili lilipochukuliwa na kuingizwa katika Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika na sasa linarejelea taaluma inayochunguza na kuchambua lugha kitaalamu.

discourses.source_txt: Waraka was also borrowed from the Arabic language ﻮﺭﻗﺔ (waraqatu). The original meaning of this word in Arabic is LEAF OF A TREE.
discourses.translated_txt: Neno waraka pia limeazimwa kutoka katika lugha ya Kiarabu ﻮﺭﻗﺔ (waraqatu). Maana ya awali ya neno hili katika Kiarabu ni JANI LA MTI.

discourses.source_txt: However, when it was borrowed and incorporated into the Swahili language, its meaning changed to refer to documents written on a piece of paper that convey certain information. In conclusion, this article examines and analyzes the various phonological changes of Arabic words that were borrowed and incorporated into Swahili.
discourses.translated_txt: Hata hivyo, ilipokopwa na kuingizwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili, maana yake ilibadilika kurejelea nyaraka zilizoandikwa kwenye kipande cha karatasi zinazowasilisha taarifa fulani. Kwa kumalizia, makala hii inachunguza na kuchambua mabadiliko mbalimbali ya kifonolojia ya maneno ya Kiarabu yaliyokopwa na kuingizwa katika Kiswahili.

discourses.source_txt: After identifying various changes, it was determined that many Arabic words were adapted into Swahili after being borrowed, with their consonants altered to simplify pronunciation for Bantu speakers. In addition, there are sounds and pronunciation patterns that were borrowed directly from Arabic without any modification. Moreover, there were also changes in meaning in some of the borrowed Arabic words incorporated into the Swahili language. Therefore, the evidence shows that both changes in meaning and pronunciation occurred in some Swahili words borrowed from Arabic.
discourses.translated_txt: Baada ya kubaini mabadiliko mbalimbali, ilibainika kwamba maneno mengi ya Kiarabu yalichukuliwa na kubadilishwa katika Kiswahili baada ya kukopwa, huku konsonanti zao zikibadilishwa ili kurahisisha matamshi kwa wasemaji wa Kibantu. Zaidi ya hayo, kuna sauti na mifumo ya matamshi ambayo ilikopwa moja kwa moja kutoka Kiarabu bila mabadiliko yoyote. Aidha, kulikuwa pia na mabadiliko ya maana kwa baadhi ya maneno ya Kiarabu yaliyokopwa na kuingizwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Hivyo basi, ushahidi unaonyesha kwamba mabadiliko ya maana na matamshi yalitokea kwa baadhi ya maneno ya Kiswahili yaliyokopwa kutoka Kiarabu.
